# Can class-weighted LoRA improve human behavior ranking?

2026-11-26 | Anicca Research

**TL;DR.** We ran 64 actual optimization steps. On 256 held-out sessions, weighted SFT achieved AUROC .624722 vs standard .464174, base .536048 and logistic .699488. Its unadjusted paired AUROC interval excludes zero versus base only. No production promotion.

![Research cover](/assets/research/manager-execution-02-weighted-sft-2026-11-26-cover.svg)
Cover: Run02 actual human purchase data, 256 test cases.

## The problem
Our previous adapter was robust to answer ordering but weak at ranking outcomes. This benchmark note is for developers familiar with Python and binary classification.

## How we ran it
1. We used the UCI Online Shoppers data (CC BY 4.0), with a seed42 split unused in our own prior pilots: 256 training cases (37 positive), 128 calibration, 256 test (42 positive).
2. On Mac mini we loaded SmolLM2-135M. Both arms used seed42, LoRA r4 alpha8 q/v projections, AdamW 3e-4, batch8 and 32 steps. Standard BCE vs positive weight 219/37=5.918919. Two answer orders in training and evaluation.
3. We saved and reloaded both adapters, with maximum prediction difference zero. Positive-slope logit calibration used only the calibration split. [Research PR](https://github.com/Daisuke134/anicca/pull/9514) contains code, weights and test predictions.
4. We computed 5,000 paired case bootstrap draws for Brier and independently recomputed five models' Brier/AUROC values, then used 5,000 stratified paired bootstrap draws for AUROC differences.

![Evaluation pipeline](/assets/research/manager-execution-02-weighted-sft-2026-11-26-pipeline.svg)
Figure 1. Fixed 256/128/256 split and actual training/evaluation, Run02 receipt.

## Results
| Model | AUROC | Brier | NLL |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| logistic | 0.699488 | 0.126989 | 0.414971 |
| weighted_cal | 0.624722 | 0.138310 | 0.450184 |
| base_cal | 0.536048 | 0.138386 | 0.450420 |
| prior | 0.500000 | 0.137207 | 0.446562 |
| standard_cal | 0.464174 | 0.137497 | 0.447476 |

![Measured AUROC](/assets/research/manager-execution-02-weighted-sft-2026-11-26-chart.svg)
Figure 2. AUROC on the same 256 cases, 42 positive, Run02 receipt.

Weighted minus base AUROC +.088674, 95% interval [.018135,.155207]; weighted minus standard +.160547, [-.008901,.323654]; weighted minus logistic -.074766, [-.168336,.021584]. Weighted minus logistic Brier +.011321, [.000160,.022789]. This is evidence of a ranking improvement in one comparison, not a win over logistic regression.

## Trade-offs and limitations
We favored a small CPU run with one training seed. Intervals condition on fixed predictions, not training uncertainty; no multiplicity correction. Team-wide and pretraining overlap are unknown. Retrospective completed-session features do not prove prospective predictions or causal effects. Official Psych-101 and product benefit remain untested. Raw weighted probabilities need calibration. No production promotion.

## Reproduce or contribute
Read [code, checkpoints and evaluation](https://github.com/Daisuke134/anicca/pull/9514), and propose matched evaluations in [our research issue](https://github.com/Daisuke134/anicca/issues/9483). See [Anicca](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6755129214) and [open metrics](https://aniccaai.com/open/).
